options.text: By reacting an acid with a metal
By mixing two soluble compounds to form a precipitate

questions.explanation: Insoluble salts are made by precipitation. Two soluble compounds are mixed together, and the insoluble salt forms as a solid precipitate. The precipitate is then filtered, washed with distilled water, and dried.

questions.stem: Which of these salts is insoluble in water?
questions.explanation: Barium sulfate (BaSO₄) is insoluble in water. Most sulfates are soluble, but barium sulfate, calcium sulfate, and lead sulfate are exceptions. All sodium, potassium, and ammonium salts are soluble, as are all nitrates.
